rows.what the ink shows: The opening high stroke turns into a small shoulder; low detached marks follow before a second tall, descending f-shaped stroke. Its long rightward connection and final small rounded mark support transforme, although the middle letters are strongly compressed.

An initial p descends below the other low marks, followed by a short a/r group, a tall crossed t, an i dot, a long low connected run, then a curved l and another dot before the final horizontal er. These visible landmarks support particulier.

The cancelled upper line preserves a crossed x at its left and an open C at its right. Dense diagonal cancellation covers the intervening character; its original bars or curvature cannot be distinguished securely enough to confirm the proposed membership sign.

The lower cancelled line retains a clear upright 1 with a foot at the left, a tall looped f with a descender, a following upright and rounded low connection for b, and a short t with a rightward cross-stroke. The diagonal cancellation traverses this group but leaves these landmarks visible.

Above the inserted x-to-1 arrow is a tall looped first stroke with a descending left side, a rounded lobe crowded against its lower right for the b, and a final separate short crossed t. The f/b strokes are tightly joined, but the abbreviation is legible as fbt.
Above C, the pointed cap has two outer sloping sides and a third stroke descending centrally from its apex. The central shaft makes this an upward arrow rather than the two strokes of a wedge.
The mark below x-to-1 has a sloping left arm, a curved right arm and a separate central downstroke that reaches below the left arm. This is an upward-pointing arrow with a shaft, not a simple wedge.
To the right of the upward arrow are three distinct small letters: a tall f crossed on the left, a b with an upright and closed low bowl, and a t with a crossbar extending right.

After the opening parenthesis, the first word has a looped l, a dot over the following i, a long low middle connection and a raised t near its right end. The next word begins with a long descending f, continues along a low stroke, then rises and bends through the b/l group before the terminal e.

The cancelled character has a small open curl on its upper left, a heavily filled upper oval crossed by ink, and a long descending stroke that encloses a small lower counter. A g is possible, but the overwritten head does not preserve a secure distinction from a looped mathematical letter.

The sign above C has an arched pointed cap, two outer downward arms and an additional central descending shaft, with a white gap separating the shaft from the left arm. These three strokes identify an upward arrow.

The abbreviation next to the lower limit begins with a looped f whose stem descends below the line, followed by a tall b returning into a rounded low connection, and a final t with a short horizontal cross-stroke.

The word begins with an open c and a small adjacent a, followed by low elongated strokes. A dot appears over the i near the right, and the following q has a pronounced descending stroke that returns into the terminal ue connection.
